_source: Town hall / city hall addresses, spot-checked against each town's own government website.
_method: A small, hand-curated pilot list — NOT a directory of all US municipalities. Each entry's `address` is a fixed, publicly-known civic building, never a visitor's own address (see GOOGLE_CIVIC_API_KEY's comment in config.py for why). fetch_town_ballot (app/pipeline/fetch/civic_info.py) calls voterInfoQuery with this address live, on a user picking the town — there is no separate pre-verification pass the way state_ballot_lookup.json's per-state links have, because a bad address here just surfaces as that town's ingest_failed on the next request rather than staying silently wrong between runs.
_note: Response field schema (contests/referendumTitle/candidates/etc.) is verified against Google's public Discovery Document (https://www.googleapis.com/discovery/v1/apis/civicinfo/v2/rest, no API key needed to fetch it) — the same machine-readable source Google's own client libraries are generated from, not a guess from prose docs. What that document can't confirm is DATA quality: whether each address below actually resolves to a useful result, which needs one real authenticated call per address the first time GOOGLE_CIVIC_API_KEY is set in a live deployment — no different from any other keyed source here needing its first real run. Expand this list by hand, the same way state_ballot_lookup.json's `states` entries are added one at a time.
